scenarios.label: Normal mission
scenarios.description: No equipment failure. Food storage stays cold for the whole 450-Sol mission, so vitamins in the packaged food degrade only at the normal rate.

scenarios.label: Small storage failure
scenarios.description: At Sol 150 the food-storage cooling fails for 45 Sols and peaks at 29.5 °C; the greenhouse goes offline. Vitamins in stored food break down faster. This is the default scenario.

scenarios.label: Major storage failure
scenarios.description: At Sol 150 the food-storage cooling fails for 60 Sols and peaks at 30 °C; the greenhouse goes offline. This is the mildest failure (searched over 60-240 Sols x 30-45 °C) in which an astronaut's vitamin B1 body store actually falls below its risk threshold.

destinations.label: Earth orbit
destinations.source_citation: Smith SM, Zwart SR, Block G, Rice BL, Davis-Street JE. The nutritional status of astronauts is altered after long-term space flight aboard the International Space Station. J Nutr 135(3):437-443 (2005).
destinations.where_in_source: Abstract: '11 astronauts before and after long-duration (128-195 d) space flight'.
destinations.note: Destination 'Earth orbit': upper end of the ISS long-duration stays in this cohort. Used only as the forecast horizon (how many Sols of the same simulation are reported); the model itself is unchanged. Converted to Sols with 1 Sol = 1.02749 days.

destinations.label: Moon
destinations.source_citation: Modelling assumption of this project (no source).
destinations.note: Destination 'Moon': no source in this repository for a crewed lunar mission length; ~30 days is an assumed order of magnitude. Used only as the forecast horizon; the model itself is unchanged.

destinations.label: Mars
destinations.source_citation: Modelling assumption of this project (no source).
destinations.note: Destination 'Mars': the simulated mission length (CrewScenario.mission_sols = 450 Sols = 462 days). Scenario design, no source. It is the default forecast horizon.
